reviews.text: 一个人做的游戏，属实是高质高量了，模型和画面非常精美，每种武器都有其特色，装甲技能多样化，再加上芯片功能的搭配，最起码能组合出好几种玩法，真是爽游中的极品，对比其它幸存者类型的游戏，难度确实不高，不过某芯片的功能，可以让喜欢挑战难度的玩家尽情娱乐，真要说有缺点的话，就是一个人做游戏更新实在太慢了，希望大卖，招点人一起开发 ^_^
比打手冲还爽！
为了解锁设计的解锁 全是负反馈 进去一堆UI都是灰的.点这个要几级解锁点那个要几级解锁. 到底图啥呀？强行限制玩家游玩顺序？拉高游戏游玩时间？这是单机游戏呀大哥 任务系统也是.等于逼人按照你设计的顺序玩.不然解锁不了后面内容 我都直接打夜晚了.非要逼我打黄昏. 一个以让玩家爽为核心的游戏模式非要做那么多添堵的设计.实在玩不下去 里面战斗体验还是可惜的.希望制作组别教人玩游戏了

首先，我是重度肉鸽爱好者，要我对这部作品的评价就是：作为一款大学生毕设作品的话，十分惊艳。但是可惜，他是一部商业作品。 怎么说呢，这游戏玩起来十分难受和鸡肋，所有的升级系统都是机械地增加数值，请问制作组你有玩下去的欲望么，肉鸽的核心不是数值升级打怪通关，而是技能和机制联动 联动 联动！！！联动造成每一把游戏的体验不同，造成肾上腺素飙升的快感，这才是肉鸽游戏的核心玩法，我玩了2小时居然打着打着睡着了，你敢信？ 这部作品每一个技能都是独立的，激光是激光，炸弹是炸弹，你打你的，我打我的，升级就是加血，加伤害，加攻速，我就问你有升级那个什么武器和机甲的欲望和兴致么？辛辛苦苦升个级，就是打怪伤害从20变成了25大哥，2023年了，如果你是第一个开发这种玩法的人，那无疑是天才之作，但现在环境是有这么多精良的肉鸽游戏珠玉在前，这作品是怎么做成这样的？每把游戏不都是一样么？升级打怪通关？除开画风（画风我很喜欢，美工老师辛苦了）这不就是个复杂一点的页游么？ 最后，我是工薪摸鱼党，拿工资支持一下国产游戏，制作组听得进去就改我多玩一会，听不进去或者改的成本太高就算了，毕竟开发一部作品真的不容易也要考虑成本，就这样。

我玩到霰弹枪的时候我真的蚌埠住了，在别的游戏里霰弹枪都是高伤害高穿透的割草大杀器，到这个游戏里变成了低伤害0穿透的烂枪，到页面看了一下，哦，枪械属性里没有初始穿透属性，原来是压根没设计，除了高斯步枪初默认全是0是吧，初始霰弹枪DPS甚至还没有初始冲锋枪高，那你设计这个武器干什么呢，甚至霰弹枪连距离伤害增强和衰减都没有，散射机枪和霰弹枪之间又是什么关系呢？ 武器平衡快重新改改吧，大部分前期低伤害武器加成这块根本就没有肉眼可见的提升，HP，攻速，移速，拾取范围这些为什么加成都比武器的的提升高呢，因为这些数值都是百位起的，唯独你个前期的武器大部分都是个十位起，而且所有的辅助武器初始伤害就比我手里的武器伤害高，捡个小蜜蜂，伤害开局就是25，加两次攻速加个数量直接就起飞了，捡个中期暴击大师好家伙我不用开枪了，举个例子散射机枪加个主武器+20%，伤害始伤害6我+20%变7，冲锋枪开局一秒十枪，专属升级里还有加弹道的，哦合着你冲锋枪，散射机枪和霰弹枪都是一样的用途是吧，我升级之前三四枪打死和我升级之后三四枪打死有什么区别吗？我真的笑了你知道吗，初始伤害数值这么低，伤害全靠暴击打，拿到暴击大师的牌就无双，拿不到就难打，这导致谁攻速高谁就厉害，所以主武器+20%，辅助武器20%，15%全局伤害这些加成有啥用 ，本身基础伤害就低，还浪费我升级机会，升级需要的经验值本身设计的就不平滑还给我升级塞一堆废品,，建议改成武器伤害+5，辅助伤害+5，全局伤害+3这种的而不是百分比。 升级系统也是没啥深度，就是一条路升级到底，说实话吸血鬼的精髓没学到位，人家那都是组合变成大杀器你这个就只有升级到底变成一个数值怪物，就纯叠数值说真的玩着不无聊吗？每局都是一样的东西，一样的升级，一样的出怪设计，真的无聊，无聊到我快睡着。 最后就是那个任务系统，我就不多说了就一句话，现在还有这样限制游戏进度的机制我是没想到的。

《贪婪大地》是一款加入了类幸存者玩法的俯视角动作射击游戏，游戏中玩家可以设置是使用类幸存者玩法的游玩方式还是类孤胆枪手的游玩方式。前者只需要玩家移动和使用技能即可，射击方面则是自动进行的，而后者则是需要自己操控射击，虽然提高了玩家需要操作的部分，但是可以自由控制例如武器的发热以及攻击目标等，能够显著提高玩家的操作上限，打出更好的成绩，如何取舍，还需要玩家自己决定。 游戏讲述了在一个充满了敌对生物的异星，玩家需要为人类开辟一块建造基地的区域，因此需要孤身与层出不穷的敌人作战并击败它们。游戏的整体难度并不高，敌人的数量虽多，但是玩家的火力更猛。玩家可以通过拾取敌人掉落的经验值来提升等级，从而在多个升级项目中选择，是加强主武器的属性还是增加辅助装备提高动力装甲的能力，玩家可以自由选择。 玩家选择战斗的地图可以在多个不同难度不同敌人的地图上进行选择，在同一张地图上还可以更改战场时间，改变敌人的强度以及收获的奖励等。玩家还可以在每个关卡地图中的三个任务中选择，加入任务会让玩家的战斗更加艰难并加入很多限制，但是同样也可以获得更多的奖励。游戏的奖励基本上分成两个，都是用来在局外解锁更多的装备以及提升已解锁的装备的等级的，在游戏中玩家就可以获得更强大的火力支援以及更多样的辅助装备随机的可能。 游戏还有一套军衔系统，玩家需要在军衔系统中完成其中的三个任务来提升军衔等级，游戏的大量内容都会被军衔系统所限制，玩家只有在提升到相对应的军衔等级的时候才能够解锁，因此玩家其实需要优先去完成军衔系统，这也是增加了游戏肝的方向和肝的内容。 总的来说，游戏的内容丰富，并且优秀的画面也让玩家的射击割草更有冲击力，也更有可玩性。丰富的肝的内容也让游戏保持了更多的新鲜感，玩起来十分上头。 [quote] 执笔勾墨色，挥毫著文章；阳春布德泽，璞玉生光辉 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44174077/]吟遊诗人的手札[/url]，书游戏特色，写游戏魅力 [/quote]

[h1]《贪婪大地》：机甲幸存者[/h1] 《贪婪大地》是一款由VaMP He开发、Gamersky Games和2P Games发行的机甲风射击向类幸存者游戏，相较于普通像素风幸存者，《贪婪大地》除了拥有丰富的内容以外，还为玩家提供了高规格的画面和机甲风的射击体验，在国产幸存者作品里也算是个有趣尝试。 [h2]最机甲射爆的一集[/h2] 在《贪婪大地》中，玩家扮演一名星际佣兵，在贪婪大地上把出现的敌人全部砍翻，开发组也不避讳游戏就是缝合了《Crimsonland》（《血腥大地》）以及《Vampire Survivors》（《吸血鬼幸存者》），或者说本身即是在这两者迭代的基础上加了点自己的构筑，虽然机甲风看上去像《血腥大地》，不过实际体验或许会更加接近《吸血鬼幸存者》一点。游戏的最大特色就是这个「星际佣兵」，在主题界面就有一股未来风满满的感觉，而玩家也可以对武器进行升级，局内还有多种成长，构筑内容还是相当丰富。 作为一个俯视角的射击游戏，《贪婪大地》其实并不是第一个将幸存者跟射击结合的游戏，今年年初有一款《僵尸幸存者》在画面表现力上比本作更强，内容也更为丰富。不过鉴于贴上了国产标签，有如今这个完成度所以也不必对其太过苛责，游戏的操作手感对我来说还能接受，也的确能打发一段无聊的时光，作为闲暇时的消遣再好不过。 [h2]底子上还是个幸存者[/h2] 对于幸存者游戏来说，最重要的还是繁多的游戏内容来让玩家觉得充实，《贪婪大地》也不例外。游戏的流程就是不断杀敌获取经验然后解锁技能，构筑出最强大的进化方向，打造出一个超级战士。本作还提供了丰富的武器库供玩家选择，提高了游戏的可玩性。 并且幸存者常见的卡屏问题本作也少不了，而且由于本作的画面规格较高，因此怪海带来的卡屏来的要更早一些，甚至基于游戏朴素的优化可能在一开始就有卡顿的感觉，敌人稍多一点就会有明显的卡帧感。不过这也是幸存者的老毛病了，庞大的怪海带来的巨大计算量会给显卡和CPU造成负担也是在所难免，如果不能优化游戏那就优化自己的电脑吧。 [h2]总结[/h2] 《贪婪大地》作为一款机甲风幸存者，很好地完成了自己的本职工作，在为玩家提供了丰富内容的同时，也拥有不错的俯视角射击体验。如果你找不到一款好的射击类幸存者代餐，那么这款游戏能为你提供一个额外的选择。 [quote] 执笔勾墨色，挥毫著文章；阳春布德泽，璞玉生光辉 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44174077/]吟遊诗人的手札[/url]，书游戏特色，写游戏魅力 [/quote]

Part of the boredom is also due to the lack of difficulty: I find little challenge in this game so far, even when I have the optional difficulty modifiers enabled for extra rewards. I'm just mowing everything down, not in a "Yeah, eat it!" sort of way, but more like a "Dear God, can we be done now?" sort of way.

[h1]Negative Reviews Were Right[/h1] [i]This is one of those games where the negative reviews turned out to be completely accurate. [/i] [h3]Repetition[/h3] The biggest problem with Greedland is how repetitive it is. Almost everything feels the same from beginning to end. The enemies barely change, the environments all look alike, the objectives repeat over and over, and even the animations get old very quickly. The audio doesn't help either. There is basically no soundtrack. The entire game has only three ambient tracks: one for the main menu, one during gameplay, and one that plays when a boss appears. That's it. There is a progression system, and to be fair, it works. Unlocking upgrades gives you a sense of progress, but it doesn't solve the core issue. The game simply becomes boring because every run feels almost identical. No upgrade system can fix that. [h3]Performance[/h3] Another major downside is the Unreal Engine implementation. The game performs poorly on both Steam Deck and PC. During the later stages, performance drops significantly, with FPS often falling well below 30 regardless of the graphics settings. On Steam Deck, I also experienced some of the longest stutters I've ever seen in a game. I'm talking about freezes lasting two or even three seconds, and again, changing the graphics settings made no difference. [h3]UI[/h3] The interface also deserves criticism. It looks like it was taken straight from a mobile game. It isn't completely unusable, but it feels cheap, low-effort, and not very polished. Another annoying issue is that controller support is broken in many parts of the UI. At first I thought something was wrong with my controller, but I quickly realized it was actually the game's fault. [h3]I can't recommend wasting your time on this one.[/h3]

So I'm sat on the fence with this one - and let me tell you, the fence is uncomfortable, splinters everywhere, the lot - so I've written you a proper essay instead of just slapping a thumbs up like some caveman who's never had an opinion in his life. Decide for yourselves, you're adults. Allegedly. Here's the stuff I actually liked. There's loads of shiny tat, so if you're a completionist, one of those poor souls who can't sleep until every little icon is ticked off - congratulations, you've found your life's work, and you won't see your family for a fortnight. It's also dead generous with loot, chucking resources at you like a drunk uncle chucking fivers at a wedding, enough to buy and upgrade your gear, though for the really pricey stuff it expects you to grind a bit. Nothing's free, is it. Not even in a game about shooting things. They've taken everything UE5 has to offer and gone absolutely mental with it, and here's the thing: you can tell the devs loved this. What they were a bit short on in the animation and rigging department, they made up for with sheer, genuine affection. Bless them. And I loved Crimsonland, so finding out this is its genuine spiritual successor - even the banner looks like its long-lost cousin - got me a bit emotional, if I'm honest. Didn't expect that on a Tuesday. Now for the stuff that got on my wick. Unless you're one of the aforementioned completionist hostages, it starts getting boring around the ten-hour mark, because the whole thing boils down to Brotato or Soustone Survivor with a posh haircut. And look -I love this genre, I'd marry it - but I wanted better level design. I know level design is hard, alright, I'm not a monster, and you can SEE them trying to make the levels and enemies look different. But mechanically? Every level's just the same level wearing a different hat, and that's what kills it after ten-ish hours. Same dog, different jumper. So why am I recommending it, then? Because the devs poured their entire hearts and souls into this thing and you can feel every drop of it. It's a good game made by people who clearly loved making it, and if you like twin-stick shooters, you'll have a proper good time. Simple as. If I were changing anything, it'd be the levels, which are monotonous as a motorway, give them their own mechanics, something to actually wrestle with on top of the usual chaos. Never built a game in my life, so I might be asking for the moon, but: limit how long you can stand in the sun in the desert levels, make you slip about in the snowy ones. Something. Anything. Make the place matter, not just the wallpaper. And a little note to the devs, lovingly: when you make a game for everyone, you make a game for no one. Was talking about exactly this with my pal Johan the other day, and he's right, the man's a sage. I'd shave off most of the bells and whistles and trade them for harder levels and meatier mechanics - instead of a dozen-plus battle suits and guns, ship me a dozen genuinely different levels, each with its own feel and its own personality. But honestly, brilliant job getting a game like this out the door, genuine kudos to all of you, and your next one could be an absolute belter if you focus on simple mechanics and proper unique levels. Worth the money, especially on sale, for a solid 10–30 hours. It needs some quality-of-life love and a bit of tidying up on the progression, but there are no major bugs or crashes, which these days deserves a parade of its own. And one last thing: if you couldn't care less about the theme and just want a game in this genre, give it a swerve. For me the theme is half the reason I enjoyed it - it's the only reason I sank ten hours in before I started moaning. Take the theme away and you've just got me, sat back on that horrible splintery fence. And nobody wants that.
